notes:
I couldn't write these notes, because the research tool stopped working before I could read anything. My first attempt to fetch the sources was rejected with a "no more tool calls remaining this turn" error, and a second try failed the same way. I didn't get any text from any of the sites.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes, since all of them would have come from memory and had no URL behind them.

These are the pages I tried to read, and I'll start with them when the tool is available again (in a new turn or session):

- **Verse-by-verse (traditional reading):** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-31/; biblehub.com commentaries on Isaiah 31 by Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Gill; the Jamieson-Fausset-Brown commentary on studylight.org; Precept Austin's Isaiah 31 page.
- **Modern scholarship:** netbible.org translator notes on Isaiah 31, especially on "pass over" (v. 5) and "fire… furnace" (v. 9).
- **Differences between traditions:**
  - desiringgod.org, gty.org and spurgeon.org (Baptist)
  - ligonier.org and monergism.com (Reformed)
  - wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes)
  - lcms.org and 1517.org (Lutheran)
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** newadvent.org (Church Fathers) and catholic.com.
- **Popular modern teaching:** gotquestions.org pages on trusting in "horses and chariots."

If you'd like, ask again and I'll do the research and write the notes in your "v. 4: …" format, with a URL for each point.
